description.value: The study examined cognitive, behavioral, and brain-volume changes across clinical severity groups in familial frontotemporal lobar degeneration mutation carriers and noncarriers.

spans.text: We compared cognitive performance, behavioral ratings, and brain volumes across groups of asymptomatic and symptomatic carriers

description.value: A cross-sectional analysis of first-time-point data from familial frontotemporal lobar degeneration longitudinal cohorts, with participants categorized by mutation status and clinical severity.

spans.text: The current analysis presents data collected at the first time point from this cohort.
Clinicians were blinded to each participant’s mutation status unless the participant had learned their mutation status.

value: Asymptomatic mutation carriers showed nearly identical scores on all clinical measures compared with noncarriers but reduced frontal and temporal lobe volumes.

source_definition.value: Disease stage was defined categorically from mutation status and clinical severity using the CDR plus NACC FTLD: asymptomatic nonmutation carriers (−mFTLD-CDR = 0), asymptomatic mutation carriers (+mFTLD-CDR = 0), mildly/questionably symptomatic mutation carriers (+mFTLD-CDR = 0.5), and symptomatic mutation carriers (+mFTLD-CDR ≥ 1).

spans.text: Cortical volumes for the frontal and temporal lobes for each individual were also calculated by transforming a brain parcellation atlas [ 18 ] into the study-specific brain space and summing all modulated gray matter within the frontal and temporal lobes.
